description: Halo! Saya pengembang web full-stack (React/Next.js) dengan minat di AI dan IoT. Sedang mencari rekan tim (Desainer UI/UX, Analis Data, atau konseptor kreatif) untuk berkolaborasi memecahkan tantangan NASA Space Apps. Mari bergabung dan berinovasi bersama!
summary:
GreatEye is an interactive, satellite-driven web dashboard designed to monitor and analyze forest and land fires (karhutla) across Indonesia. To overcome data fragmentation caused by differing sensor specifications, we developed a data harmonization pipeline that integrates active fire (hotspot) datasets from NASA FIRMS—specifically MODIS (Terra & Aqua) and VIIRS (Suomi-NPP)—spanning from 2023 to 2026. Using Spatial Grid mapping and DBSCAN density-based clustering, the system transforms raw, multi-sensor thermal anomalies into a unified, consistent geospatial reference.

Indonesia faces an escalating wildfire crisis driven by human activities and climatic factors, often overwhelming disaster response teams. GreatEye addresses this challenge by eliminating cross-sensor bias and duplicate hotspot counts, enabling stakeholders—such as BNPB, the Ministry of Forestry, firefighters, researchers, and the general public—to accurately visualize historical trends and pinpoint high-risk fire zones. This tool is crucial for shifting disaster management from reactive firefighting to proactive, data-driven prevention and early warning.
details:
GreatEye harmonizes multi-sensor satellite data and presents it through an interactive geospatial web dashboard. Because MODIS captures larger pixels (1 km) while VIIRS captures finer spatial details (375 m), a single fire event often registers as multiple hotspots in VIIRS compared to MODIS. Our backend pipeline resolves this discrepancy through a four-step harmonization methodology:

  1. Temporal Standardization: Merging acquisition dates and times (acq_date and acq_time) and converting timestamps from UTC to Western Indonesian Time (WIB, UTC+7).
  2. Intersecting Window Alignment: Trimming raw datasets to a uniform observation period (January 1, 2023 – August 1, 2026 WIB) to prevent timeframe bias, resulting in 106,795 aligned MODIS records and 507,934 VIIRS records.
  3. Confidence Level Standardization: Mapping MODIS’s continuous numeric confidence scores (0–100) into VIIRS’s discrete categories (l for low [0–29], n for nominal [30–79], and h for high [80–100]).
  4. Cross-Sensor Validation & Clustering: Aggregating daily counts, validating temporal consistency via Pearson correlation ($r = 0.8819$), and applying Spatial Grid and DBSCAN clustering to group dense hotspots into actionable high-risk fire zones.

Users can explore the harmonized data via interactive maps, filter hotspots by date range and region, and analyze historical time-series trends.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Technical & Data Integrity: Eliminates cross-sensor bias and duplicate counts, providing a single, clean, and reliable dataset for researchers and analysts.
  • Operational & Disaster Mitigation: Empowers firefighting and disaster management agencies (BNPB, BPBD, Manggala Agni, Ministry of Forestry) to distinguish isolated fires from large-scale clusters, optimize logistics, and prioritize patrols in red zones before peak dry seasons.
  • Public Awareness & Education: Translates complex remote-sensing metrics into an intuitive visual interface, helping local communities monitor nearby fire threats and haze risks while serving as an open learning reference for students and academics.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

  • Data Source: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System) active fire archives (MODIS C6.1 and Suomi-NPP VIIRS C2).
  • Data Science & Backend Processing: Python (pandas and numpy for tabular/time-series manipulation, geopandas and shapely for geospatial processing, scikit-learn for DBSCAN clustering, and plotly/matplotlib for analytical validation).
  • Frontend & Deployment: ReactJS and TypeScript (leveraging component-based architecture, Virtual DOM for smooth rendering, and static typing for GeoJSON spatial structures), deployed on Vercel.

Creativity & Team Considerations

Rather than simply plotting raw satellite coordinates—which often misleads users due to VIIRS's higher detection sensitivity—our team focused on scientific rigor and usability. Combining statistical correlation validation with spatial density clustering (DBSCAN) ensures that visual spikes represent true fire intensity rather than sensor artifacts. Additionally, we prioritized local operational relevance by standardizing all timestamps to WIB (UTC+7)and designing a responsive, low-barrier UI accessible to both technical policymakers and everyday citizens.
